heading: INT. BRIGHTWATER ANIMAL CLINIC - EXAM ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. BRIGHTWATER ANIMAL CLINIC - EXAM ROOM - DAY
CLOSE ON a stainless steel table, a tabby cat on a towel, a stethoscope sliding across its ribs.
Fluorescent hum.

DR. PRIYA NAIR, 34, sharp-eyed, hair in a hasty knot, scrubs with a faded cartoon dog on the pocket, works the stethoscope while TOMAS REYES, 36, a carpenter in a flannel shirt with sawdust still in the seams, holds the cat's head with both hands as if it were a bird's egg, and the whole small white room, the poster of canine dental anatomy, the jar of tongue depressors, the window onto a parking lot where rain is just beginning, waits for her verdict.
Heart's fine. Lungs are clear. She's just old, Tomas.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: She's thirteen.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: That's old for a cat who eats my pens.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: ANGLE ON Tomas.
He almost laughs.
She ate one pen.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: It was a Montblanc.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: INSERT - THE CAT'S CHART.
Name: BISCUIT.
Owner: T. REYES.
Last visit: eleven months ago.
A sticky note in Priya's handwriting reads, "Ask him about the dinner."
BACK TO SCENE
Priya sees him see it.
She flips the chart closed.
This is the last time they will be alone in this room, though neither of them knows it yet.
You wrote that after I cancelled.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: I write a lot of things.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Priya.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: It's fine. I got over it. I have a very busy schedule of getting over things.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: WE SEE her hand shaking just slightly as she caps the stethoscope, and him noticing, and neither of them saying so.
My mother was sick. That's why I cancelled. I should have called.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: You did call. Three months later.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: I know.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: A beat.
Biscuit purrs, loud, unashamed.
Is your mother okay?
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: She passed in March.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Priya's face changes.
All the armor goes out of it at once.
Tomas. I'm so sorry.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: I wasn't telling you for sympathy. I was telling you because you should have been told. A long time ago.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: The door swings open without a knock and WENDY OKAFOR, 20s, vet tech, bleach-blond ponytail, a clipboard hugged to her chest and a golden retriever puppy on a leash tugging her sideways, pulls up short at the sight of the two of them standing a foot apart.
Oh. Sorry. Dr. Nair, Mrs. Halloran's here with the Great Dane and she says it's an emergency but it's the same emergency as Tuesday.
units.name: WENDY

units.text: Give me two minutes.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: She said that's what you said on Tuesday.
units.name: WENDY

units.text: Wendy.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Going. I'm going.
units.name: WENDY

units.text: The puppy scrambles in a circle, tangling the leash around Tomas's boots.
He crouches to free it, and Wendy stands there a second too long, reading the room the way a young person reads a room, with enormous obviousness.
Come on, Waffles. Let's give the grown-ups the room.
units.name: WENDY

units.text: She tows the puppy out.
The door clicks.
CLOSE ON the doorknob, still turning, then still.
Tomas stands with a tangle of leash in his hand that no one is holding anymore.
Have dinner with me. Not a date. Just dinner. I'll pay and I'll answer anything you ask.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Anything?
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Anything.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Why did you take eleven months to bring her back in?
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Because every time I picked up the carrier I thought about walking in here and seeing you, and I didn't know what face I had.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Silence.
Rain on the window now, steady.
Biscuit stretches a paw toward the edge of the table and Priya catches her without looking.
Thursday. I get off at seven.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Thursday.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Bring the cat. She's the only one who ever told me the truth about you.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: He smiles, finally, a real one, tired and relieved, and scoops Biscuit into the carrier as Priya holds the door.
For a moment they both stand in the doorway, too close, the narrow frame making them one shape, and in the hallway behind them Mrs. Halloran's Great Dane begins, mournfully, to howl.
That's my emergency.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Go.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: She goes.
He stays a moment longer in the empty exam room, looking at the wet window, at the last line of the chart, at the sticky note he has not been supposed to read, and he is smiling at nothing.
